## The spec had never been generated

Before any implementation was possible, the spec had to parse — it never had. Six defects, all mechanical:

| Defect | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Specification: Bowling` | `Specification` takes no colon |
| `Detail Roll is between…` | keyword is `Details` |
| `Given rolls are  # Pins` (line 42) | `#` is a comment, so the table had no block — `: Pins` |
| ValidValues column `Valid` | must be `IsValid` |
| `Then Then tenth frame values are` | duplicated keyword, which became a `Then_Then_…` glue method |
| `Roll` and `Score` field types | **see below** |

That last one is the interesting one. `FrameValues` typed its fields as `Roll` and `Score`. `Score` is never declared anywhere, and `Roll` is a `DomainTerm`, not a DataType. The generator emitted `FrameValuesTyped` with fields of those types and String assignments into them — **code that cannot compile**. I typed the roll fields as `Pins` (which is what `DomainTerm Roll : Pins` already says they are) and declared `DataType Score`.

Worth knowing: the analyzer accepts a DomainTerm as a field type, but the generator can't produce a conversion for one and emits broken code instead of erroring. That inconsistency is a converter gap — say the word and I'll file it in `Remaining Work.txt`.

## What I implemented

Production, in `src/main/java/bowling/` — all the scoring lives here, none in the glue:

- **`Pins`** — 0–10 or `TBR`; throws `NumberFormatException` out of range, which is what the generated DataType test requires
- **`Score`** — a score or `TBS`
- **`Frame`**, **`FrameMarks`**, **`InputControl`** — scoresheet values
- **`BowlingGame`** — frame boundaries, scoring, marks, the two-row display, completion, and next-roll control

The glue only hands rolls in and compares what comes back. The display check is a literal string comparison against the spec's text block, not a parse-and-rebuild.

The rule I had to read out of the expected data: `Roll1..Roll3` are the three rolls **starting at** the frame's first roll, not the frame's own rolls — frame 4 is a strike and still lists the next two. Score is `r1+r2+r3` for a strike or spare, `r1+r2` otherwise.

## Two things to know

**Gradle can't run this.** The wrapper is 7.5.1, which can't run on JDK 24, and JDK 11 (your `JAVA_HOME`) can't compile the text blocks the generated test uses. Only those two JDKs are installed. I compiled with JDK 24 directly and ran via the JUnit Platform launcher, using the JUnit jars already in your `.m2`. To make `gradlew test` work you'd need a JDK 17 toolchain or a newer wrapper — I didn't change your build files.

**Nothing is committed.** That repo has *no commits at all* — everything was staged but never committed, so there was no baseline to fall back on. I left it that way. The spec is now restored and corrected at `specs/bowling.spectable`; it had been empty, with the content surviving only in a deleted git blob in `specstudio` and a stale worktree.

## What the glue does

No production code — the API is the thing under test.

- **`Given base Page is`** stores the base; `When sending request` joins it to `Page` with exactly one slash.
- **Request bodies** come from the `Given` steps via the generated **`toJSON()`** (`NewPostTyped`, `ReplacePostTyped`, `PatchTitleTyped`), keyed by attribute-set name so `| Body | NewPost |` resolves.
- **The call** is `java.net.http.HttpClient` — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
- **The response** goes back through the generated **`fromJsonValue()`** into `ResponseTyped` / `PostItemTyped`, then every field the spec states is checked.

`string` and `number` are treated as **type assertions**, not literals — the spec uses them where jsonplaceholder returns lorem ipsum not worth pinning. Blank and `?DNC?` assert nothing; everything else must match exactly.

## Three changes to API.spectable — please review

Two were structural, and without them nothing could run:

1. **`Attributes Request` declared only `Method` and `URL`.** Every `Page` and `Body` row in the scenarios was being **silently dropped** — five of six scenarios reached the glue with an empty URL. Now `Method`, `Page`, `Body`, and scenario 1's `| URL | posts/1 |` became `| Page | posts/1 |`.
2. **`| Page | =BASERUL/posts |`** — typo for BASEURL, and no such `Define` exists. Since the Background already supplies the base, this is now just `| Page | posts |`.
3. **DELETE's `| Body | {} |` removed** — the one genuine value mismatch. The API returns `200` with `{}`, an empty object carrying no fields, so `body` came back empty. I left a comment there: `Response.body` means the post's body *text*, which isn't what `{}` is. **Whether that scenario should assert the raw payload instead is your call** — I didn't invent a mechanism for it.

Also worth knowing: `ResponseTyped.fromJSON` can't be used directly on a response, because it calls `Json.require(m, "status")` and no API response body contains `status` — that's the HTTP status code. The glue injects the real status into the parsed map before handing it to `fromJsonValue`, and fills fields the API omitted with type-correct defaults (`0` for ints, `""` for strings) since `require` rejects absences and `asInt` rejects `""`.

**One recurring trap hit twice:** regenerating API wiped `TableHelper.java` both times and broke the build, exactly as the new `Remaining Work.txt` warns. I re-ran the union after each regeneration. That will keep happening until the generator is fixed.

The headline: **Karate collapses the spec and the glue into one file.** Everything we just built — `RestCall`, `API_glue`, the generated `*String`/`*Typed` classes — is what Karate ships as its DSL. For pure API testing you write no Java at all.

The same scenario:

```gherkin
Scenario: Retrieve a single post
  Given url 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com'
  And path 'posts', 1
  When method get
  Then status 200
  And match response == { userId: 1, id: 1, title: 'sunt aut facere...', body: '#string' }
```

Two things there are worth noticing, because you arrived at both independently:

- **`path 'posts', 1`** — Karate's `path` takes segments, not a joined string. That's exactly the `Page` / `Parameter` split you asked for. Karate does the joining, as `RestCall.send` now does.
- **`status` is its own step**, separate from `match response`. That's the status/body split you asked for, and for the same reason: they come from different places.

And `'#string'` is Karate's built-in **fuzzy matcher** — so the `string`/`number` placeholders Copilot wrote aren't a wrong idea, they're an unformalised version of a real Karate feature (`#number`, `#boolean`, `#notnull`, `#uuid`, `#regex(...)`). The difference is that Karate makes them explicit syntax you can't confuse with a literal, whereas a bare `string` in a table cell is indistinguishable from expecting the word "string". That ambiguity is exactly what let the unverified expectations hide.

| | SpecTable | Karate |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | General specs → 9 languages | HTTP/API testing specifically |
| Glue | You write it | None — the DSL is the test |
| Assertion | Field-by-field, generated typed classes | `match` on a whole object, deep/nested |
| Typing | Declared `Attributes` with types | Dynamic JSON |
| Arrays | One row checked per item, by hand in glue | `match each response ==` built in |
| Non-API domains | Bowling works fine | Not what it's for |

Where each wins is fairly clean. **Karate** is far less work for API testing — our `RestCall` plus glue is maybe 250 lines that Karate gives away, and `match response == {...}` in one line replaces `checkPost`'s four comparisons plus the placeholder logic. **SpecTable** is doing a different job: it isn't API-specific, it generates the same spec into nine languages, and its declared types mean `Post` is checked structurally rather than as loose JSON — which is why the Bowling spec works in the same tool.

The honest read on this particular file: if `API.spectable` were the whole job, Karate would be the better tool. Its value here is as a *demonstration* that SpecTable can reach a live service — and the glue is now small enough to show that in one screen.

Worth a look at Karate's `match each` if you keep the array scenario — it's the one place our approach is clearly clunkier, looping 100 items in the glue to apply one row.

### Assistant

Verified. For an exact set you **do** list them — that's the case where `match each` doesn't apply:

```gherkin
Scenario: Retrieve posts for one user
  Given url 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com'
  And path 'posts'
  And param userId = 1
  When method get
  Then status 200
  And match response ==
  """
  [
    { userId: 1, id: 1, title: 'sunt aut facere...', body: 'quia et suscipit...' },
    { userId: 1, id: 2, title: 'qui est esse',       body: 'est rerum tempore...' }
  ]
  """
```

`match ==` on an array is a **deep and order-sensitive** comparison of the whole thing — extra elements, missing elements, or a different order all fail. The triple-quote docstring is just for readability; a one-line array literal works identically.

If the expected set is large or reused, you externalise it:

```gherkin
And match response == read('user-1-posts.json')
```

Two related forms: `match response contains any read('some-items.json')`, and `match response !contains { status: 'deleted' }`. There's also `contains only` for "exactly these, order irrelevant" — I believe that's the keyword, but the reference I pulled garbled its example, so treat that one as unconfirmed.

## Where this flips the comparison

This is the case where **SpecTable's notation is the better one.** An array of objects *is* a table:

```
Then response posts are : Post
| userId | id | title             | body              |
| 1      | 1  | sunt aut facere.. | quia et suscipit..|
| 1      | 2  | qui est esse      | est rerum tempore |
```

That's more readable than the JSON, it's diffable line by line, and a missing or extra row is visually obvious. Karate's docstring is just JSON pasted into a feature file.

But **SpecTable can't currently say it.** `Then response array items match` applies one row to *every* element — there is no step meaning "the array is exactly these rows, in this order." So the exact-set assertion you're describing is expressible in Karate and not in SpecTable today, even though SpecTable has the better notation for it.

That sharpens the array gap into three distinct things rather than two:

| | Karate | SpecTable |
|---|---|---|
| One shape, every element | `match each` | ✅ current step |
| Exact set, in order | `match response == [...]` | ✗ |
| One element by index | `response[0]` | ✗ |

One caveat if you build it: jsonplaceholder's bodies are multi-line, and a table cell holds one line — the same limit that stopped me pinning `body` earlier. Karate's docstring has no such problem. An exact-set table step would need an answer for multi-line cell values, or would be limited to specs whose values are single-line.

Both entries in `specstudio/Remaining Work.txt` are now corrected. To answer directly:

**CompareOnly — yes, you're right.** `: Post CompareOnly` fills every column the table omits with `?DNC?`, and both the generated `equals` and my glue's `check()` skip `?DNC?`. So a table listing only id and title checks exactly those two. That also means the two placeholders still in `API.spectable` aren't needed:

```
And response body is : Post CompareOnly
| id | title |
| 1  | sunt aut facere ... |
```
drops `| body | string |` entirely rather than asserting a type. One restriction: the step regex is `:\s*(\w+)(?:\s+(Vertical|CompareOnly))?` — one modifier only, so `Vertical CompareOnly` won't parse. An exact-set table is horizontal anyway, so it only bites a single-object check that wants both.

**Define-as-multi-line — right idea, but it doesn't work today.** Both halves exist independently: the parser accepts a docstring Define (`State::InDefineDocString` sets `hasDocString`), and a cell accepts `=Name`. They just aren't joined. `resolveValue` resolves an `=` reference *only* for a scalar Define, and the guard excludes exactly the case you want:

```cpp
if (d.name.compare(name, ...) == 0 && !d.isTable && !d.hasDocString)
```

A docstring Define referenced from a cell falls through to `resolveCell` and the cell keeps the literal text `=X`, which then fails against real data. Docstring Defines are reachable from a bare step (`step.hasDocString` → looks the Define up) but not from a table. Same guard verbatim in `CppGenerator.cpp:29` and `CSharpGenerator.cpp:28`, so it's likely all nine.

Relaxing it — and emitting the text the way a step docstring already is (Java text block, escaped literal elsewhere) — would make jsonplaceholder's four-line bodies comparable. That's now written up in Remaining Work as a concrete change rather than a language limitation.
